02 / 16

The problem: AI wants to live where the data is, and nobody builds small

SMBs face a cloud bill that grows with success, colocation priced for hyperscalers, or a server closet nobody commissioned.

  • Wholesale colocation about $196 per kW-month in US primary markets (CBRE, H2 2025)
  • Traditional builds $10–13 M per MW and 18–30 months (Cushman & Wakefield 2025)
  • Modular vendors optimise for telcos and hyperscalers, not a 40-person manufacturer or a clinic
  • Later: the 2 MW regional center for enterprises, hospitals, universities, municipalities and edge colocation, which the same system already sizes and prices (BEN 2000)
  • BEN 2000 infrastructure-only about $10,200 per kW vs $10,000–13,000 per kW traditional (BOM-based)

Speaker notes

All three numbers are cited in docs/investors/MARKET_SOURCES.md with ranges. Say the ranges out loud; investors respect ranges more than point estimates. Transition: the product family. The BEN 2000 figure comes from docs/BOM-ben2000.md and scripts/unit_economics.py (infrastructure-only sell price $16.4 M for 1,600 kW IT); say 'about $10,200 per kW infrastructure-only vs $10,000–13,000 per kW traditional' and that most of that BOM is quote-only estimates.

One engineering model from a 0.6 kW mini rack on a shelf to a 700 kW liquid-first 40 ft module. BEN 2000 shows the same system at 2 MW.

  • BEN 1 (new): indoor mini rack, 10-inch up to 0.6 kW or 12U sound-damped up to 1.5 kW, 120 V plug-in, built in-house

04 / 16

Density

As dense as a sealed, relocatable box allows, with every figure generated from the configuration and checked against real footprints, not taken from a brochure.

  • BEN 300: 150 kW per rack, 20.3 kW per m² of module footprint, 2 racks in one 20 ft frame (310 kW verified maximum)
  • BEN 700: 140 kW per rack, 23.6 kW per m², 5 racks; power, UPS, CDUs and controls in one 40 ft box (705 kW verified maximum)
  • Sourced peers: Delta 20 ft AI container up to 60 kW per rack (AC), ZTE prefab 40 kW per rack, HPE AI Mod POD up to 1.5 MW (AC)
  • Liquid-first at W45: dry coolers carry the liquid heat; a small trim chiller serves the ≤ 10 % residual air; about 177 LPM per GB300-class rack at 45 °C (vendor table)
  • Planned as BEN 1000: power gear takes 5.0 m of the 11.5 m row, so 5 racks fit and the tier carries the power that fits. Design values until measured; 800 VDC a gated study

Speaker notes

Figures from docs/DENSITY.md (generated from the configuration, 2026-11-09): BEN 300 2 x 150 kW on 14.77 m2; BEN 700 5 x 140 kW on 29.72 m2. The 40 ft tier was planned as BEN 1000 and renamed by fit (docs/REV2_DECISION.md section 2a): say so, it is the proof that the checks are real. 2N profiles drop to 155 kW (BEN 300) and 400 kW (BEN 700). Peer figures come from docs/research/STATE_OF_THE_ART_2026.md section 3 and are vendor statements, so say 'as published'. The honest positioning: every DC-ready offer is MW-class and every sub-MW container is AC; none publishes leak-to-isolation or redundancy-proof numbers. Our density is a design value until the lighthouse.

Mini racks: AI for tiny businesses

A tiny business can run private AI on a shelf: one or two AI boxes, a NAS and a firewall, plugged into the wall, set up and watched by Schreiber AI.

  • rack10: 10-inch 8U shelf rack up to 0.6 kW; cab12: 19-inch 12U sound-damped cabinet (CX Mini class, ~550 mm deep: short-depth servers only) up to 1.5 kW
  • 120 V plug-in on a dedicated 15 A / 20 A circuit; heat to room 649–1,599 W; est. 45–47 dBA at 1 m; no pad, permit or crane; 2–3 weeks to handover
  • Built and burned in by Schreiber AI, the one in-house build; noise, heat to room and UPS runtime measured before it ships
  • Risks in plain words before the price: heat in the closet, circuit overload, noise, theft, untested backups, UPS battery age
  • Market size: our sources hold no statistic for on-premises tiny-business AI; the 10-unit lighthouse is the first evidence

Speaker notes

The buyer is the owner of a studio, a trades business or a small office who wants AI on their own data without hiring IT. What they get is the same discipline as the big units: a site check, a burn-in, measured noise and heat, a handover, BEN Care watching it and a four-line owner maintenance list. Do not quote a market number for this segment; MARKET_SOURCES.md says none was found. Prices come from docs/rev2/UNIT_ECONOMICS.md.

06 / 16

Element-proof and hardened

Every unit is NEMA 4X / IP66 and hose-tested; H2 and H3 are priced packages that turn a bespoke engineering project into a catalog option.

  • H1 Standard (included): IP66 envelope, hose test per UL 50E written into the warranty, C3 coating
  • H2 Severe environment: flood plinth, marine C5-M coating, dust filtration, hurricane hardware, 67 m/s wind; auto-recommended for coastal, desert, arctic, high-altitude sites
  • H3 Hardened / government: UL 752 ballistic panels, ASTM F3038 forced-entry doors, mantrap, tamper detection, optional HEMP shield (MIL-STD-188-125-1), CMMC controls pack
  • Margin lever: hardening lines carry margin above the 35 % project base because the buyer pays for a certified, tested envelope and a compliance pack, not steel

Speaker notes

Hardening is a margin lever and a market opener (public sector, defence, utilities, coasts). Never say bulletproof, EMP-proof or TEMPEST certified: say UL 752 level, MIL-STD-188-125-1 option, TEMPEST-ready. Vendor certificates are required with every shipment (SUPPLIER_TERMS.md).
Schreiber AIBEN EngineInvestor briefingRev 206 / 16

Why we win: the configuration-driven engineering system

Drawings, bill of materials, compliance pack, assembly instructions, digital twin and commissioning report all come from the same configuration.

  • config.py sizes power, cooling, structure, mass, PUE; validate() rejects layouts that do not fit
  • 42 issue-for-construction sheets across five tiers (7 per tier, 14 for the BEN 2000 hall) with CTQ/CTP tables, regenerated from the configuration
  • Assembly instructions in ASD-STE100 for workers with minimal experience
  • Commissioning script: 12 steps (two forward-architecture steps skipped with the reason on AC units), signed report, SHA-256 of the data

Speaker notes

This is the moat. A competitor can buy the same container and UPS. They cannot buy the system that makes every unit identical and testable with few engineers. Demo backup: docs/proposals/ shows a full customer proposal generated by one command. Transition: show the twin.

08 / 16

You can run the box before it exists

The dashboard that ships in every unit runs in simulation mode: 3-D twin, walkthrough, automated sweeps, fault injection, calibration, CFD, CSV export.

  • Six automated sweeps pass on the BEN 150 preset in under a second of compute
  • Ride-through sweep shows thermal, not battery, is the binding limit (about 2 minutes to ASHRAE A2 max with cooling off) — this drove the mechanical ride-through option
  • Calibration tools produce GUM uncertainty budgets per sensor

Speaker notes

Live demo plan: bash scripts/run_dashboard.sh, open localhost:8080, change tier to BEN 500, inject a cooling failure, watch the standby unit start, run the failover sweep, download the CSV. Recovery plan if the demo fails: the screenshots in docs/media/screens and the sample commissioning report. Caveat to say out loud: the twin's thermal time constants are design values, so the two-minute number is a lower bound until measured on hardware.
Schreiber AIBEN EngineInvestor briefingRev 208 / 16

09 / 16

Compliance is the product

The compliance pack is generated per mission profile; it already changed the design three times.

  • A2L refrigerants are unusable inside a container at these charges: in-row DX specified with R-513A/R-515B (A1, GWP < 700) ahead of the AIM Act 2027 rule
  • NFPA 855 / UL 9540 triggers at 20 kWh lithium: BEN 5/30/150 stay under it by default; BEN 500 carries the full package
  • NEC 110.26 at 480 V drives an electrical vestibule on BEN 150/500
  • IEC 62443 zones; life safety hardwired and never on the controls network
  • BEN 2000 is a building: IBC permit, MV service, NFPA 855 battery rooms, NFPA 110 Level 1, SPCC; hardening adds UL 50E / UL 752 / ASTM F3038 / MIL-STD-188-125-1 rows

Speaker notes

Investors in this space have been burned by permitting. Lead with the three findings that changed the design; they prove the matrix is not decoration. Edition years are listed in docs/COMPLIANCE.md with what could not be verified.
Schreiber AIBEN EngineInvestor briefingRev 209 / 16

Business model and unit economics

Prices are built up from a real bill of materials with a confidence split, not top-down.

  • BEN 150 preset (96 kW): infrastructure-only sell price about $0.71 M; all modules including reference GPU compute about $2.9 M at 35 % gross margin
  • Underlying BOM cost is 79 % vendor-confirmed listings, 21 % engineering estimate (BEN 150); every line carries its status
  • Recurring: BEN Controls licence per unit per year and managed service at $45 per kW-month (below retail colocation because the customer owns the asset)
  • Rev 2 sell prices at 35 % gross margin on the whole project: BEN 1 rack10 $21,873, cab12 $64,739 (with reference compute); infrastructure-only BEN 300 $1.43 M, BEN 700 $2.52 M, BEN 2000 $9.0 M

Speaker notes

The exact table is regenerated by scripts/unit_economics.py into VC_PROPOSITION.md. Be explicit that 'confirmed' in this session means a distributor listing seen in search results on 2026-11-07, not a quote; the 21 RFQ emails queued to Ben@SchreiberAI.com convert those into quotes. Compute dominates the all-modules price; most SMB customers will start infrastructure-only.

What is verified, what is not

We tell investors the same thing we tell customers.

  • Verified here: configuration model, twin, CFD, calibration, sweeps, commissioning (simulation), BOM generator, drawings, firmware unit tests on host, product page render
  • Implemented, unverified: EFR32 Pod cross-build (toolchain blocked), edge computer image and PLC project, Pod attestation, all hardware behaviour
  • Least accurate: thermal ride-through minutes, envelope UA, CFD absolute temperatures, estimate-status prices
  • Rev 2 tiers (BEN 1, BEN 300, BEN 700) are design values from the configuration; no Rev 2 hardware exists until the lighthouse units
